source.title: Large-Scale Power Plant String Inverter Market to Reach USD 8.91 Billion by 2034 as Utility-Scale Solar Deployment Expands
source.body:
Global Large-Scale Power Plant String Inverter Market is estimated at USD 5,742.00 million in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 6,029.10 million in 2026. According to Energy Resources Insights, the market is expected to reach USD 8,907.73 million by 2034, representing an assumed compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.0% during 2026–2034. Market development is supported by expanding utility-scale photovoltaic installations, increasing demand for high-capacity power conversion equipment and the adoption of advanced inverter architectures across large solar projects.

Large-scale power plant string inverters convert direct current (DC) electricity generated by photovoltaic modules into alternating current (AC) electricity suitable for grid integration. These systems are increasingly relevant to utility-scale solar installations requiring flexible power conversion, distributed maximum-power-point tracking and improved performance across different module configurations. The market covers first-sale revenue from string-format DC-to-AC inverters deployed in large ground-mounted power stations, excluding central inverters, rooftop equipment, transformers, engineering, procurement and construction services, and maintenance contracts.

Market at a Glance

·         2025 market size: USD 5,742.00 million

·         2026 estimate: USD 6,029.10 million

·         2034 forecast: USD 8,907.73 million

·         Forecast CAGR: 5.0% during 2026–2034

·         Leading region: Asia-Pacific, based on the report's indicative regional assessment

·         Key equipment category: High-power utility-scale string inverters

Utility-Scale Solar Expansion Supports Market Development

The expansion of global solar photovoltaic capacity is an important demand factor for large-scale power plant string inverters. According to the International Energy Agency, global solar photovoltaic additions exceeded 600 GW in 2025. Increasing investment in utility-scale solar generation creates opportunities for manufacturers supplying high-capacity inverter systems designed for large installations.

High-power string inverters provide project developers with greater flexibility in managing different photovoltaic array configurations. Their distributed conversion architecture can support installations with uneven terrain, varying module orientations and different shading conditions. Equipment selection depends on power rating, conversion efficiency, grid-support functionality, operating temperature and maintenance requirements.

The 250–350 kW category represents an important commercial equipment range. Products such as Sungrow SG350HX, Huawei SUN2000-330KTL-H1, GoodWe UT and SolarEdge TerraMax demonstrate the technical development of high-capacity utility string inverter solutions.

Key Market Drivers and Challenges

Several factors are influencing the industry's development:

·         Utility-scale solar installations: Expanding photovoltaic generation projects create demand for high-capacity inverter equipment and associated grid integration technologies.

·         Advanced power conversion: Higher-power string inverter designs support improved system configuration and distributed maximum-power-point tracking.

·         Grid integration requirements: Compliance with grid codes, reactive power capabilities and grid-support functionality influence purchasing decisions.

·         Project optimization: Developers evaluate inverter architecture according to installation conditions, cable requirements, operating efficiency and lifecycle costs.

·         Repowering opportunities: Replacement and modernization of existing solar infrastructure create additional demand for updated inverter technologies.

However, the market faces challenges associated with price competition, equipment reliability, grid connection requirements and the selection of string versus central inverter architectures. Inverter pricing pressure can also affect revenue growth even as equipment shipments increase. Project developers must evaluate warranties, operating temperatures, cybersecurity requirements and long-term maintenance support before selecting suppliers.

Segmentation and Regional Outlook

The market is segmented by power rating, grid architecture, project type and installation category.

·         Power rating: Below 250 kW, 250–350 kW and Above 350 kW.

·         Grid architecture: 1500V DC string and Other Utility String.

·         Project type: Ground-mounted Utility Solar and Floating and Agrivoltaic Utility Solar.

·         Installation: New-build and Repowering.

Asia-Pacific is positioned as the leading regional market in the report's assessment, supported by China's significant solar deployment activity and the presence of major inverter manufacturers. China remains an important manufacturing and installation center, while India represents another relevant market for utility-scale photovoltaic development.

Europe offers opportunities through large solar installations, grid modernization and demand for advanced grid-compliant inverter systems. North America is supported by utility solar investment and renewable electricity expansion. South America and the Middle East & Africa also present opportunities as solar generation capacity develops.

Regional revenue shares are indicative analyst scenarios rather than independently audited market statistics.

Competitive Landscape

The competitive environment includes established photovoltaic inverter manufacturers developing high-power string inverter platforms. Key companies covered in the report include Sungrow, Huawei, GoodWe, SolarEdge and Fronius.

These companies compete through equipment efficiency, power ratings, grid integration capabilities, product reliability and technical support. Manufacturers are increasingly emphasizing higher-capacity equipment, advanced monitoring functionality and solutions compatible with utility-scale photovoltaic installations.

The availability of products in the 320–350 kW range demonstrates the industry's movement toward high-capacity string inverter configurations. However, product availability does not independently establish global manufacturer revenue shares.
